instructions: In the image at screenshot: Is there text set directly on a busy photo or pattern, where the detail behind the letters makes the text hard to pick out?

criteria.true: Some text sits directly on a busy, detailed photo or pattern with no panel, overlay, or shadow behind it, so the detail behind the letters breaks them up and makes the text hard to pick out.
criteria.false: Text over images sits on a calm area of the image, or on a panel, overlay, or shadow that keeps it easy to read, or no text is set over an image or pattern.

instructions: In the image at screenshot: Is there text or a shape in one vivid, saturated colour set directly on another vivid colour of about the same lightness, so that the edge between them seems to flicker or vibrate?

criteria.true: Text or a shape in one vivid colour sits directly on a different vivid colour of about the same lightness, so the edge between the two colours seems to flicker or vibrate and is tiring to look at.
criteria.false: Wherever one colour sits on another, the two clearly differ in lightness, or at least one of them is a neutral or muted colour, so no edge seems to flicker.

instructions: In the image at screenshot: Is the accent colour, the one strong colour meant to mark the main action or the most important item, used on so many elements that nothing stands out?

criteria.true: The strong accent colour is spread over many elements, such as headings, icons, borders, backgrounds, links, and buttons, so it no longer points to one important thing.
criteria.false: The accent colour appears on only a few elements, such as the main action and one key highlight, so those elements stand out, or the page has no accent colour.

instructions: In the image at screenshot: Is a large area of the page, such as a full-width band, a sidebar, or the whole background, filled with a vivid, fully saturated colour instead of a muted, light, or dark one?

criteria.true: A large area of the page, such as a full-width band, a sidebar, or the whole background, is filled with a vivid, fully saturated colour.
criteria.false: Large areas of the page use neutral, light, dark, or muted colours, and vivid colours appear only on small elements such as buttons, icons, or highlights.

instructions: In the image at screenshot: Does the page use many different hues that do not seem to belong to one palette, so the colours look random instead of planned?

criteria.true: The page uses many different hues on its elements that do not seem related to each other or to any role, so the colours look random instead of planned.
criteria.false: The page uses a small, related set of colours, such as a neutral base with one or two accents, so the colours look planned.

instructions: In the image at screenshot: Are elements that do the same job, such as the buttons in one row or the cards in one grid, shown in different colours from each other for no visible reason?

criteria.true: Elements of the same kind that do the same job, such as matching buttons or cards side by side, are each shown in a different colour, and nothing about them explains the difference.
criteria.false: Elements that do the same job share one colour, and where colours differ the difference marks a different role, state, or category that the page makes clear.

instructions: In the image at screenshot: Are two or more different vivid colours given equal weight on the page, each on large or prominent elements, so that no one colour leads and they compete for attention?

criteria.true: Two or more different vivid colours each cover large or prominent elements at about the same size and strength, so no single colour leads and they compete for attention.
criteria.false: One colour clearly leads and any other colours are smaller, quieter, or neutral, or the page uses only one vivid colour.
